extracted.intended_audience: teachers, educators, and those interested in pedagogy and moral education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for teachers/parents on using bodily sensations, emotions, social feelings, and punishments as motives in education and discipline; describes which motives to employ, how to temper them, and pitfalls to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual food regimen as a motive
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Having in view the necessities of discipline with the young, the habitual regimen in food should be pitched neither too low nor too high to permit of such variations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Food is a major motive: distinguish privation (deficiency of nourishing material) from stomachic hunger (local craving). Small, understood privations (e.g., skipping a meal) may be an effective motive without harming vigor; absolute diminution of nutrition is severe. Poverty limits use of this means; where unavailable, physical punishment becomes a fallback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of physical punishments (caning, flogging) — power and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The inflictions of caning and flogging... are a powerful deterring influence... the limitations to its use demand a rigorous handling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical acute pains produce strong deterrence but are classed among organic pains (injury to tissue) and can be destructive if carried far. They are widely used historically but require strict limits and careful consideration of long-term harms and moral consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer sensory pleasures as incentives; avoid sensory punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The ordinary five senses contain... considerable sensibilities to pleasure and pain. The pleasures can be largely made use of as incentives. The pains... very rarely are.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit pleasures of taste, touch, sight, hearing, and smell as rewards. Avoid using unpleasant sensory experiences as punishment (bad odors, bitter tastes, harsh sounds), which are uncommon and inappropriate means of discipline; painful sights are relegated to barbarous codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for higher emotions as motives
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Postponing a review of the principles of punishment generally, we approach the most perplexing department of motives — the higher Emotions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher emotions (social emotions, anti-social feelings, intellectual gratifications, pleasures of action, self-esteem, fear) are powerful motives; educators must analyze and use them appropriately rather than relying solely on simple sensational incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage intellectual pleasures; manage intellectual pains
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Both the delights of attained knowledge and the pains of intellectual labor have to be carefully counted with by every instructor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make use of the gratification from learning to motivate study while acknowledging and mitigating the discouragement or fatigue that accompanies difficult intellectual work (e.g., by staging tasks, offering recognition, and varying activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pleasures of action/activity as motivators
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The pleasures of Action or Activity are a class greatly pressed into the educational service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide opportunities for active engagement, practical tasks, and constructive activity to harness the intrinsic satisfaction of doing as a stimulus for learning and good conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use self-esteem, pride, praise as educational motives
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The names Self-Esteem, Pride, Vanity, Love of Praise, express powerful sentiments... To gratify them is to impart copious pleasure; to thwart or wound them is to inflict corresponding pain.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise and opportunities for esteem can strongly motivate children. Use them to reward desirable behavior but avoid humiliating or needlessly wounding pride; cultivate personal dignity alongside social approbation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear/terror should be last resort; avoid superstitious terrors
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In the higher moral education, the management of the passion of fear is of the greatest consequence... it should be reserved for the last resort.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate moderate predictable consequences from terror. Small, well-defined privations may be preventive without producing fear. Severe or uncertain punishments induce terror, paralyzing action and scattering thought. Avoid spiritual/ghostly/superstitious terrors (e.g., frightening children with ghosts or other-life threats). Refined forms of fear (e.g., tragic sympathy) may be artistically useful when tonally appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust discipline to temperament (timidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Timidity, or susceptibility to fear, is one of the noted differences of character; and this difference is to be taken into account in discipline.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize individual differences: timid children may respond to governance in some ways (preventing commission) but not to others (remediating omissions). Long-term bad usage can create timidity; set realistic expectations and adapt methods (support, gradual exposure, encouragement) for timid natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate sociability and social motives
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The pleasures of love, affection, mutual regard, sympathy, or sociability, make up the foremost satisfaction of human life... It would appear strange if this motive could ever be overlooked by the educator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harness social motives — friendship, mutual regard, parental and sexual affections, broader sympathetic feelings — as central incentives. Use cooperative learning, friendship-based encouragement, and the desire for approbation to foster study and moral development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use friendship and small-group attachments for deep culture
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The favorable conjunction for study and mental culture in general is friendship between two, or a small number... each naturally smitten with the love of knowledge for its own sake.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage small peer groups or friendships founded on shared intellectual interests to promote sustained, high-quality learning beyond mere social conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage collective/social context but beware mediocrity
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In the presence of an assembly the individual is roused... The tendency is to secure a certain approved level of attainment... If there were no other strong passions called out in society, the general result would be... mediocrity and dead level.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class teaching and mass settings stimulate individuals to reach group standards (drill, public performance). Use this to raise low performers but guard against an undue leveling effect that suppresses individual excellence; combine mass instruction with opportunities for individual distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel anti-social and malign emotions; cultivate sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In the work of discipline the present class of emotions occasions much solicitude. They can... be turned to good account; but, for the larger part, the business of the educator... is to counterwork them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counter anger, hatred, and malevolence by fostering sympathies and affections, appealing to personal dignity, and explaining long-term consequences. Use social disapproval and the cultivation of concern for harm done to others as checks on malign impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide safe outlets for competitive/malevolent impulses
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Total repression has been found impossible; and ingenuity has devised a number of outlets that are more or less compatible with the sacredness of mutual rights.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow controlled outlets (competitive games, regulated contests, disciplined conflict with rules) and institutionally limited vengeance (legal punishment administered privately) to absorb some malevolent drives while preventing real harm. Avoid glorifying revenge in stories or public punishments that feed vindictiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use play to balance destructive impulses
rubrics_metrics.description: 'By submitting in turn to be victimized, a party of children can secure, at a moderate cost to each, the zest of the malevolent feeling; and this I take to be the quintessence of play.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage play and role-playing that simulate destructive impulses in a controlled, reciprocal fashion (sham biting, play-fighting) to allow expression without injury, but monitor to prevent escalation into real harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate expression of anger — measured indignation as discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There is a fine attitude of indignation against wrong that may be assumed with the best effect. It supposes the most perfect self-command... Neither containing fitfulness, nor conducting to excess of infliction, it is the awe-inspiring personation of justice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If anger or indignation is employed, it must be self-controlled, proportionate, and consistent to serve as a moral example and deterrent. Uncontrolled fitfulness undermines discipline and breeds inconsistency in sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conquer superstitious fears via scientific education
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The conquest of superstitious fears is one of the grandest objects of education... It cannot be accomplished by any direct inculcation; it is... one of the incidental... results of the exact study of Nature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce irrational/spiritual terrors by cultivating scientific understanding and exposure to nature; indirect cultural change through inquiry and knowledge is more effective than direct admonition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep punishments private to limit public vindictiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The privacy of the punishments of criminals, in our modern system, is intended to keep the indulgence within bounds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer penalties without public spectacle to avoid stimulating collective vindictive pleasure; privacy constrains public indulgence in retribution and helps maintain focus on reform rather than revenge.
